definitions.explanation: A positive impression of a person, thing, or event. Often used when evaluating someone's character or behavior in social or professional settings.

examples.japanese: {好印象|こういんしょう}を{持|も}つ。
{彼|かれ}の{礼儀正|れいぎただ}しい{態度|たいど}に{好印象|こういんしょう}を{受|う}けた。
examples.english: I received a favorable impression from his polite manner.

examples.japanese: {面接|めんせつ}{官|かん}に{好印象|こういんしょう}を{与|あた}えるために、{身|み}だしなみに{気|き}をつけた。
examples.english: I paid attention to my appearance in order to give the interviewer a good impression.

notes:
A compound of {好|こう} (good, favorable) and {印象|いんしょう} (impression). Frequently used when discussing interpersonal evaluations, job interviews, and social interactions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {好印象|こういんしょう}を{与|あた}える — to give a good impression
- {好印象|こういんしょう}を{持|も}つ — to have a good impression
- {好印象|こういんしょう}を{受|う}ける — to receive a good impression
- {好印象|こういんしょう}を{抱|いだ}く — to harbor a favorable impression

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {第一印象|だいいちいんしょう}: first impression — specifically about the initial encounter
- {悪印象|あくいんしょう}: bad impression — the opposite
